newsitem.title: BRAZIL: End of ICMS tax seen boosting Brazil agribusiness.
newsitem.headline: End of ICMS tax seen boosting Brazil agribusiness.

text.p: The elimination of an export tax on primary and semimanufactured goods is expected to give further boost to Brazil's agribusiness sector, a report by Fator Securities said.
The bill exempting exports from the so-called ICMS tax, which is levied by state governments, has already been approved by the Chamber of Deputies and goes for a vote today in the Senate.
Fator's report said the sector is already benefitting from a rise in prices for main agricultural products on the international markets.

But once the bill becomes law "there should be an immediate effect on the production chain due to higher demand for low-cost agricultural goods such as fertilizers and seed, which are most purchased seasonally in the second half of the year," the report said.
It also noted "the consumption of higher priced durable goods like machinery and tractors should occur at a later stage as the agricultural sector grows in the medium term."

Considering the positive effects of the ICMS tax exemption, Fator said it was recommending investors buy stocks of Fosfertil, a producer of raw materials for fertilizers, and Manah, a NPK mixing company.
